Requirement applicability: SystemCtx explicitly identifies a ReadIndex operation; ReadyToRead denotes readiness for a prior batch; the consumer selects that exact context. The obligation applies when the leader releases an admitted remote record, not to every pending request or a success deadline. Legal prefix: Launch constructs three fresh regular Peers and bootstrap entries. The driver stores entries/state before exposing messages, applies only actual committed configuration/noop entries, acknowledges updates and reports applied indexes. It ticks node 1, routes generated vote and replication messages, and checks all members know leader 1, have applied commitment beyond bootstrap, and the leader has current-term commitment. Output records term 2 and commit 4. TestLogDB is a no-crash storage substitute; transport is a serial deterministic queue. No role, log, remote match, pending read, or acknowledgement is fabricated. The chosen finite schedule delays earlier contextual heartbeat messages and delivers the later actual heartbeat and generated reply; it does not require simultaneous handler execution. Producer continuity: Peer.ReadIndex on nodes 2 and 3 produces actual forwarded requests; admissions inspect the live leader pending records, requiring stored requester/context to match issued values. The one-response quorum includes leader 1 and actual voter 2 in a three-voter configuration. Source confirm then releases the prefix; the observed suffix has zero pending records and two replies. Independent correlation: (scenario, requester) uniquely selects one admission for each output; requester is read from response To, not the compared context, and no expected-context equality filters outputs. CA_EVENT results are copied from actual exported message fields; destination ReadyToRead is independently read from Peer.GetUpdate after Handle. The monitor has no applicability exclusion and compares the full Low/High context string against admit.expected_context. Actual observations: single requester 2 retains 101/1001 at index 4. In overlap, requester 2 was admitted with 201/2001 but received 202/2002; requester 3 was admitted with and received 202/2002. Both destination ReadyToRead observations carry 202/2002. The monitor correlated all three results, reports no parser errors or missing results, and marks the requester-2 overlap comparison violated. This answers the original remote-prefix identity question in a generated stable-term history. Source attribution agrees: confirm returns stored records, but the remote emission branch uses triggering m.Hint/m.HintHigh rather than each s.ctx. The local branch and single-outstanding-request path are protective alternatives; the successful control is retained and does not contradict the scoped overlapping-prefix defect. Finite undelivered traffic is explicit and the stopping point is independent of equality. No claim of lost automatic continuation, client timeout, stale application data or global consensus failure follows from this measurement.

feedback.answered: Initial A1/A2 relationship: leaders append term/index-qualified entries, aggregate match indexes over remotes and witnesses, and request log commitment with the current term. Followers qualify replication by predecessor term, bound advertised commitment by the received suffix, and return replication support. Candidate authority is acquired through distinct votes after log freshness and vote guards; higher terms normally reset authority, lower-term messages are ignored, and reset clears votes, pending read confirmations and remote progress while preserving log history. Campaigns are blocked while committed work remains unapplied because membership may be pending. Membership application changes the quorum universe and removal can step down the leader or recalculate commitment. Snapshot handling distinguishes already committed, matching-log and actual restore cases; remotes are reconstructed separately. Engine updates send only Replicate/Ping before SaveRaftState; ordinary responses follow persistence. Ready-to-read consumption remains conditional on the matching local batch and applied index. A sourced discrepancy remains: readIndex.confirm releases a prefix of stored contexts, but handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation sends each remote destination the triggering message context instead of that released item's stored context, whereas local completion uses the stored context. No overlapping legal history or endpoint has been executed. An initially suspicious absence of an observer check in heartbeat response consumption is insufficient: broadcastHeartbeatMessageWithHint sends nonzero contexts only to voters. Peer.Handle also rejects responses from unknown members, and candidate vote handling rejects observers.

Requirement applicability: SystemCtx explicitly identifies a ReadIndex operation; ReadyToRead denotes readiness for a prior batch; the consumer selects that exact context. The obligation applies when the leader releases an admitted remote record, not to every pending request or a success deadline. Legal prefix: Launch constructs three fresh regular Peers and bootstrap entries. The driver stores entries/state before exposing messages, applies only actual committed configuration/noop entries, acknowledges updates and reports applied indexes. It ticks node 1, routes generated vote and replication messages, and checks all members know leader 1, have applied commitment beyond bootstrap, and the leader has current-term commitment. Output records term 2 and commit 4. TestLogDB is a no-crash storage substitute; transport is a serial deterministic queue. No role, log, remote match, pending read, or acknowledgement is fabricated. The chosen finite schedule delays earlier contextual heartbeat messages and delivers the later actual heartbeat and generated reply; it does not require simultaneous handler execution. Producer continuity: Peer.ReadIndex on nodes 2 and 3 produces actual forwarded requests; admissions inspect the live leader pending records, requiring stored requester/context to match issued values. The one-response quorum includes leader 1 and actual voter 2 in a three-voter configuration. Source confirm then releases the prefix; the observed suffix has zero pending records and two replies. Independent correlation: (scenario, requester) uniquely selects one admission for each output; requester is read from response To, not the compared context, and no expected-context equality filters outputs. CA_EVENT results are copied from actual exported message fields; destination ReadyToRead is independently read from Peer.GetUpdate after Handle. The monitor has no applicability exclusion and compares the full Low/High context string against admit.expected_context. Actual observations: single requester 2 retains 101/1001 at index 4. In overlap, requester 2 was admitted with 201/2001 but received 202/2002; requester 3 was admitted with and received 202/2002. Both destination ReadyToRead observations carry 202/2002. The monitor correlated all three results, reports no parser errors or missing results, and marks the requester-2 overlap comparison violated. This answers the original remote-prefix identity question in a generated stable-term history. Source attribution agrees: confirm returns stored records, but the remote emission branch uses triggering m.Hint/m.HintHigh rather than each s.ctx. The local branch and single-outstanding-request path are protective alternatives; the successful control is retained and does not contradict the scoped overlapping-prefix defect. Finite undelivered traffic is explicit and the stopping point is independent of equality. No claim of lost automatic continuation, client timeout, stale application data or global consensus failure follows from this measurement.
